mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within two months signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals a weakening demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are adversely affected.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a quarter signals a strong supply-side expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as increased production boosts corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment (CPIAUCSL growth < 2% YoY) combined with a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 2%) signals a supportive monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real rates remain low.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) for three consecutive months signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% within a month signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it indicates broader economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 3% YoY signals a strong economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are positively impacted.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances following a 3% YoY GDP increase, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.
